mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand for new homes, signaling strong economic activity and supporting corporate earnings growth, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST exceeds 700 (current value) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate decline below 0.15% signals active monetary easing, reducing equity discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 0.15%, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 40% of cases over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) signal tightening labor market conditions, driving wage pressures and corporate profit expansion for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth below 0.5% monthly indicates supply constraints, reducing inventory availability and increasing corporate pricing power for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO growth rate is below 0.5%, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth above 0.3% monthly is associated with negative SPX 5d returns in more than 55% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth exceeding 2.5% annualized signals robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings expectations for positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2.5%, SPX 60d returns are negative in more than 45% of periods over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL growth above 2.0% annualized signals accelerating inflation, triggering expectations of monetary tightening that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL growth rate exceeds 2.0%, SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) increases indicate broad consumer demand, strengthening corporate revenue outlook for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both increase, SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods over the last 5 years.
